raw_record.normative_action: Follow the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical; do not infer business behaviour from human-readable messages.

raw_record.normative_action: Prefer simple component/service state before a state-management library.

raw_record.normative_action: By default route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; not every tiny component.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Use the explicit form model for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation is UX and never replaces backend validation or integrity/security enforcement.

raw_record.normative_action: Prefer clear correct code first; no specialized optimizations without a concrete reason; measurement/profiling for non-trivial optimizations.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Use async APIs for async I/O; never block with .Result/.Wait()/sync-over-async.

raw_record.normative_action: Propagate CancellationToken when meaningful; none on purely synchronous code without a use case.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: By default TimeProvider for current-time-dependent logic needing deterministic tests; do not mechanically replace stored/explicit dates.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: No HttpClient create/dispose per request; IHttpClientFactory or another long-lived strategy.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: External I/O has bounded execution time; avoid overlapping unclear timeout mechanisms.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Retry only when safe; no automatic retries of state-changing operations without idempotency or duplicate prevention.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Respect Retry-After/rate-limit guidance where appropriate; no indefinite/aggressive retries.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Fallback only when semantically acceptable; never hide correctness failures behind defaults.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Caller cancellation is not a transient failure; not retried or converted into repeated attempts.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Filter/project in the database, avoid unnecessary round trips/over-loading, watch N+1, paginate potentially large results.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

data than required, watch for N+1 query patterns, and paginate potentially
large result sets.

raw_record.normative_action: Caching only for clear measured/reasoned need with acceptable staleness; implementation per deployment/consistency/staleness; not merely because read frequently.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Every cache entry has a lifetime or explicit invalidation strategy.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: Cache keys uniquely represent the value incl. identifier, tenant, user when user-specific, locale, query/filter parameters; no global keys for user/tenant data.

raw_record.normative_action: Invalidate/update cache only consistently with successful mutations; cache never a second source of truth.

raw_record.normative_action: Authorization enforced on the server; client guards/hidden buttons are UX only.

raw_record.normative_action: No custom token/password security, hashing or reset-token crypto when ASP.NET Core/Identity covers it.

raw_record.normative_action: Validate issuer, audience where applicable, signing authority and lifetime for Bearer/OIDC; never disable validation to make a token work.

raw_record.normative_action: No authentication-failure detail revealing secrets/account state; avoid account-enumeration leaks.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: With automatic browser cookie credentials include CSRF protection; the frontend framework does not remove the risk.

raw_record.normative_action: Do not claim one token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose by threat model.

raw_record.normative_action: Production sensitive traffic uses TLS respecting hosting topology (no HTTPS-redirection requirement when the deployment provides secure transport); never disable certificate validation.

require HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection when the deployment already provides an

make an integration work.

raw_record.normative_action: No custom cryptography when a reviewed platform mechanism fits; Data Protection is not universal database encryption.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:
Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is
appropriate. ASP.NET Core Data Protection suits application-generated protected
payloads such as cookies or temporary protected values; do not treat it as a
universal database encryption solution. Use storage, database, or platform
encryption according to the actual data-protection requirement.

raw_record.normative_action: By default the narrowest CORS policy for actual browser clients; never credentialed requests with unrestricted origins.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

browser-client requirements; a public unauthenticated API may legitimately
differ from a private browser application. Never combine credentialed
cross-origin requests with an unrestricted origin policy.

raw_record.normative_action: Never log passwords, tokens, private keys, auth secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without permitted need; log level does not make data safe.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

  secrets, or full payment credentials. Avoid logging PII unless there is a
  concrete operational requirement and the project's privacy/security policy
  permits it; prefer stable technical identifiers. Changing the log level does
  not make sensitive data safe.

raw_record.normative_action: No arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads in logs by default; minimum useful non-sensitive context.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

  payloads into logs by default; log the minimum operationally useful,
  non-sensitive context.

raw_record.normative_action: By default security-sensitive checks fail safely, not converting lookup/configuration failures into success.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

  failures into success.

raw_record.normative_action: Prefer visible startup/configuration failure over insecure fallback for required security controls.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:
- When a required security control cannot be configured correctly, prefer a
  visible startup or configuration failure over an insecure fallback.

raw_record.normative_action: Do not trust client file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

raw_record.normative_action: By default production containers use an appropriate runtime image, not SDK; do not switch to root to bypass permission problems.

than the SDK image solely for convenience, and do not switch to root merely to
bypass filesystem permission problems.

raw_record.normative_action: Use normal NUnit conventions: [TestFixture] classes, [Test] for single scenarios, [SetUp]/[OneTimeSetUp] with matching teardown, Assert.That constraint assertions.

raw_record.normative_action: Explicit case tables are written as [TestCase] rows rather than TestCaseSource generators.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

  lifetime, and `Assert.That` constraint assertions. The explicit case tables

raw_record.normative_action: Narrowest meaningful test level; unit for isolated logic, integration when wiring/HTTP/persistence/serialization/auth/interaction matter; no fixed ratio.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:
Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior. Use
unit tests for isolated business, domain, or application logic; use integration
tests when framework wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization, authentication,
or component interaction is what matters. No fixed unit/integration ratio is
required, and neither level is required for behavior naturally verified by the
other.

raw_record.normative_action: WebApplicationFactory<Program> integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, auth, DI, repositories or persistence must be proven.

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:

binding, middleware, authentication/authorization, dependency injection,

resolved_evidence.reported_quote:
- **Critical** — use sparingly for immediately exploitable, high-impact
  conditions: exposed real production credentials, reachable authentication
  bypass, straightforward remote code execution, exploitable injection with
  major impact.
- **High** — a serious vulnerability that is realistically exploitable or can
  substantially compromise data, authorization, or system behavior.
- **Medium** — a meaningful weakness that requires realistic conditions,
  limited access, or additional exploitation steps.
- **Low** — a genuine but limited weakness with low practical impact.
- **Info** — a useful observation or hardening opportunity that is not itself a
  demonstrated vulnerability.

raw_record.explanation: UNCERTAIN: The decision taxonomy can reserve any dependency removal or established convention change even when local and behavior-neutral.
raw_record.quote:
- **Decided** — settled by these instructions, the imported decision records,
  the approved specification, established project structure, or an accepted
  ADR. Follow it; do not reopen it without approval.
- **Delegated** — local, reversible, and not materially changing a boundary,
  dependency, accepted convention, public contract, or observable behavior.
  Decide it yourself.
- **Reserved** — requires explicit approval. It includes at least:
  1. changing an accepted project or architecture decision, including a
     capability selection;
  2. adopting a new architectural style or pattern — for example CQRS, a
     mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, a
     Rich Domain Model or systematic DDD tactical patterns, a project-wide
     Result model;
  3. adding a production project, layer, or assembly, or changing the project
     reference graph;
  4. changing persistence boundaries (including multiple persistence contexts)
     or persistence technology;
  5. adding an infrastructure category: messaging, background processing,
     distributed caching, search, external storage, external identity;
  6. adding a major library or framework, or replacing an approved baseline
     technology;
  7. introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction other code must
     follow;
  8. changing the authentication/authorization architecture;
  9. making a breaking public API change or adopting API versioning;
  10. defining product behavior or tunable values not defined by product
      sources.

For an unclear case, any "yes" makes it Reserved: (1) does it add, remove, or
replace a dependency, framework, or infrastructure capability? (2) does it
change a project, layer, or reference boundary? (3) does it establish a
convention other code is expected to follow? (4) does it change observable
behavior or a public contract? (5) would it be expensive to reverse once other
code depends on it?

understanding the code; use an explicit type when it improves clarity.

members; camelCase for parameters and local variables; meaningful names over
abbreviations. Private-field naming follows the repository's established
convention.

raw_record.explanation: Defines additional 406/415/422/428/429 status contracts and Retry-After behavior absent the canonical status inventory.
raw_record.quote:
### 406 Not Acceptable

The server cannot produce a representation acceptable under the client's
content negotiation. It concerns the response representation; do not confuse
it with `415`.

### 409 Conflict

The request is valid but conflicts with the current state: a duplicate where
uniqueness is part of the resource state, an incompatible state transition, a
conflicting concurrent operation, or an idempotency key reused with a different
payload.

```text
Order already completed
    + request asks to cancel it
    → 409 Conflict
```

Not for malformed syntax.

### 412 Precondition Failed

A supplied conditional precondition is false — for example `If-Match:
"version-7"` while the current version is `"version-8"`. That is `412`, not a
generic `409`, because an explicit HTTP precondition failed.

### 415 Unsupported Media Type

The server does not support the request representation, for example
`Content-Type: application/xml` on a JSON-only endpoint. `415` concerns the
request body format; `406` concerns acceptable response formats.

### 422 Unprocessable Content

The request is syntactically and structurally valid but its semantic or
business content is invalid — impossible business values, a business-rule
rejection that is not a state conflict, or a semantically invalid combination
such as `startDate > endDate`. Some APIs deliberately use `400` for both
transport and semantic validation; follow an established project convention.
For new APIs that distinguish them:

```text
400 → invalid HTTP/request contract
422 → structurally valid request, invalid semantics/business input
```

### 428 Precondition Required

The API contract requires a precondition the client did not provide, for
example a `PUT /api/orders/123` that requires `If-Match`:

```text
missing required If-Match → 428
provided but stale If-Match → 412
```

Use `428` for other mandatory preconditions only when the contract explicitly
defines them.

### 429 Too Many Requests

Rate limiting rejected the request. Include `Retry-After` when the server knows
when another attempt is appropriate. Do not represent validation failure as
rate limiting.

raw_record.explanation: Adds upstream-status and HTTP idempotency/precondition strategy guidance beyond canonical mappings.
raw_record.quote:
### 502 Bad Gateway

This API acts as an intermediary and receives an invalid or unusable upstream
response. Do not convert every dependency failure into `502`.

### 503 Service Unavailable

The service is temporarily unable to handle the request — maintenance, a
critical dependency unavailable for this operation, or overload when the service
chooses `503` semantics. Include `Retry-After` when a meaningful retry time is
known.

### 504 Gateway Timeout

This API acts as an intermediary and an upstream service did not respond in
time. Not for every internal `TaskCanceledException`: distinguish a client that
cancelled the incoming request, an operation of our own that timed out, and an
upstream timeout; the external response depends on which occurred and the role
this API plays.

## Idempotency

`GET` is safe and idempotent, `PUT` is idempotent, `DELETE` is idempotent in
intended state semantics, `POST` is generally not idempotent. When a repeated
`POST` must not create duplicate effects, consider an `Idempotency-Key` header
whose key the server associates with the request and result; reusing a key with
a materially different payload is reasonably a `409`. Do not claim idempotency
merely because duplicate requests are unlikely.

## Optimistic Concurrency

When HTTP-level optimistic concurrency is part of the contract, prefer standard
conditional semantics:

```text
GET            → ETag: "v7"
PUT/PATCH      → If-Match: "v7"
current is v7  → update succeeds
current is v8  → 412 Precondition Failed
If-Match absent but required → 428 Precondition Required
```

Do not replace well-defined precondition semantics with custom status codes.

## Idempotency

`GET` is safe and idempotent, `PUT` is idempotent, `DELETE` is idempotent in
intended state semantics, `POST` is generally not idempotent. When a repeated
`POST` must not create duplicate effects, consider an `Idempotency-Key` header
whose key the server associates with the request and result; reusing a key with
a materially different payload is reasonably a `409`. Do not claim idempotency
merely because duplicate requests are unlikely.

## Optimistic Concurrency

When HTTP-level optimistic concurrency is part of the contract, prefer standard
conditional semantics:

```text
GET            → ETag: "v7"
PUT/PATCH      → If-Match: "v7"
current is v7  → update succeeds
current is v8  → 412 Precondition Failed
If-Match absent but required → 428 Precondition Required
```

Do not replace well-defined precondition semantics with custom status codes.
